notes: Street furniture and road decals the Road Kit places (PLAN.md 3.6c, point_furniture.py is the one reader).
`kit` is the downloaded kit the pieces come from; each asset is a normalised kit piece (metres, +Y up, forward -Z).
A piece is stood on its own lowest point (`lift` added on top), turned so its -Z runs along the road, and scaled by `scale` [x, y, z] in its own axes.
`collide` puts an oriented box of the piece's footprint into the piece's collision (a StaticBody3D after import).
Distances are metres; `back` distances are measured from the stop line (the lane's end at a junction mouth) back along the approach.
`exclude_roads` lists road-name globs an asset is never placed on (a planter or a manhole does not belong on a mountain pass).
An asset may name its own `kit` (a res:// folder ending in /) when its piece is not in the default kit.
`collide_pole` [half width, height] puts a box round the pole only -- for a piece whose arm reaches over the road, where a box of the whole footprint would stand across the carriageway.

signal / lamp / lamp_twin are the Japanese signal and road lighting poles built by blender/tools/build_street_poles.py from the Zombie Apocalypse kit (CC0). A junction is signalised when any mouth is authored traffic_light, or (signal_all_junctions) when signal_min_arms arms have arriving traffic.

`breakable` {mass kg, break_speed m/s, respawn s} makes a collide_pole piece a knock-down pole (PLAN.md 3.11): it leaves the static collision proxy, and WorldBaker gives its batch a BreakableProps node that builds one collider per pole, knocks a pole down under a car at or above break_speed (the car keeps m_car / (m_car + mass) of its speed) and brings it back after respawn seconds where nobody sees it.
Edit and rebuild: the Road Kit digest salts this file and every piece it names, so a change here rebuilds every road piece.
